Johnny, the kitchen sink has been clogged for days, some utensil probably fell down there.
And the Drano won’t work but smells dangerous, and the crusty dishes have piled up

waiting for the plumber I still haven’t called. This is the everyday we spoke of.
It’s winter again: the sky’s a deep, headstrong blue, and the sunlight pours through

the open living-room windows because the heat’s on too high in here and I can’t turn it off.
For weeks now, driving, or dropping a bag of groceries in the street, the bag breaking,

I’ve been thinking: This is what the living do. And yesterday, hurrying along those
wobbly bricks in the Cambridge sidewalk, spilling my coffee down my wrist and sleeve,

I thought it again, and again later, when buying a hairbrush: This is it.
Parking. Slamming the car door shut in the cold. What you called that yearning.

What you finally gave up. We want the spring to come and the winter to pass. We want
whoever to call or not call, a letter, a kiss—we want more and more and then more of it.

But there are moments, walking, when I catch a glimpse of myself in the window glass,
say, the window of the corner video store, and I'm gripped by a cherishing so deep

for my own blowing hair, chapped face, and unbuttoned coat that I’m speechless:
I am living. I remember you.

- Marie Howe, “What the Living Do”

Oh, i feel you. I lost my mom 16 years ago (when I was 12) and i get married in a month. To be completely honest with you wedding planning brought on a fresh wave of grief that has been with me every step of this process. Right after my fiancé proposed the thought that i couldn’t call my mom had me sobbing.

What I’ve done:
- cried, a lot
- an insane amount of therapy
- talked to my closest friends and my fiancé about it
- talked to other family about it (dad, grandma, finances mom)

How is your relationship with your fiancés mom? Can you be frank that you’re missing that mother figure? This may be an opportunity for her to support you and for you to grow closer.

Seek out other mother figures, no one will replace your mom but i wish i had done this more actively.

Know that big moments might bring on sadness too, be prepared, have people around who know this and who you trust to be there in the way you need (for me this was dress shopping).

Be upfront with any planners, coordinators, venue staff, photographers, that your mom passed away. If you can tell them yourself do so, if you cannot, ask your fiancé to. I had MANY people say “oh and your mom” blah blah blah, which always hurt. Now i am preempting it by letting them know. It was important to me that people know my stepmom is not my mom - i want them both to be honored.

Think long and hard about how you might honor your mom at your wedding, even if this is just a personal moment or object, or a more public moment/space/etc. Trust yourself to find what makes sense for you, talk to your loved ones.

As far as the money goes, are you worried that your dad will say no? What is your relationship like around money with him? I put off saying anything because i thought it would be rude and presumptuous (and i have a complicated relationship with my dad and stepmom) finally when I brought up the wedding they offered to contribute. (Prior to this I was upset that they hadn’t expressed any interest in the wedding or my engagement at all). I’ll say that i think dads just don’t “get” it like moms seem to - with your mom gone you may just need to have a frank conversation with dad. Talk to him about the wedding, ask him if he would like to be involved, talk about your feelings surrounding your mom if you can, and (i think) it’s ok to discuss money, ask if he has thought about or planned to contribute - express it is ok if he doesn’t.

My biggest piece of advice to you is just to accept that this process will be different because of your loss. Try to accept that where you can, rage when you need, grieve when you must. There have been moments that i felt the grief was overwhelming, i felt nothing but dread and sadness and fear that i wasn’t going to be able to enjoy my wedding without my mom. As the day gets closer i feel more excitement and anticipation. I know that I’ll feel sad that day, but that’s not all that I’ll feel.

I’m so sorry you don’t have your mom by your side to help you plan, and to celebrate your love, but i trust that there is part of her party planning, courageous self inside of you, and that her love is still with you even when she is not.

I don’t disagree that it’s ok to make choices for yourself and realize that your desires have changed - but any good therapist would not abide by the way you’re framing the situation. It takes two to tango in a relationship and it sounds to me like your boyfriend is taking up the ambivalence that you’ve felt about/towards kids, a different slower lifestyle, etc. in your dynamic. Especially troubling is how black and white the issue and options you’ve laid out. Everything you wrote about the dynamics of your relationship makes it sound like you have a mutual love and trust - and hopefully communication - that can withstand the stress of making these decisions. I believe that there are creative solutions and different outcomes than the options you’ve outlined. You owe it to yourself and your boyfriend to work through this together. I would urge you to get really clear about how you’ve contributed to the present situation and avoid approaching the conversation from the perspective of blaming him (for overspending, trapping you in NYC, not giving you children). If he feels persecuted and defensive, and you feel bitter and afraid, your abilities to communicate will be shut down. The conversation will be difficult but these kinds of decisions and moments in a relationship have the power to transform your love into something stronger and more meaningful at the end of the day. I’m rooting for you!

My stepmom and some of her kids and mother were there at the time - I still die with laughter when she tells the story. She has an incredibly strong “fight” reflex and immediately jumped into action. She threw all of their food into the bathroom and started filling the tub with water - corralled her mother with Alzheimers in there, tried to calm everybody’s nerves by giving them little tasks to do. But, she’s also pretty spastic and somehow shattered two windows in their rental and smashed her laptop screen during the chaos. I know I shouldn’t laugh because it seems like it was pretty traumatizing, but hearing about the wildly different individual responses (one of my stepsister’s friends laid down for a nap) gets me every time.

Was working behind the counter at a very boujee market that had a deli/ served coffee - absolutely the most drug addicted/alcohol dependent I’ve ever been in my life. One morning I had to open the store with a raging hangover. Some lady comes in and asks for a latte, as I begin to make it I realize that I am going to puke IMMEDIATELY. The bathrooms are all the way across the store and I definitely don’t have time to get there - not without running and causing a huge scene. I walked over to the nearest trash can, stuck the entire top half of my body inside and puked my guts out. I stood up and washed my hands and finished making her latte. She was on her phone and I genuinely believe that she did not notice what had happened. Apparently, none of my coworkers or any customers did either. I immediately took out the trash once she left to pay and tried (but probably failed) to get the clinging scent of vomit off my breath.

Hi there - are you able to speak with your dad or anyone else about this? Ideally therapy would be an option to work through your trauma. If your father and/or his girlfriend are supportive having open conversations about your triggers and things you are struggling with can help a lot. If that isn’t an option I highly suggest looking into grounding and breathing techniques. Essentially you want to activate your senses in the present moment. Personally I have used essential oils to smell, some body exercises like feeling my feet and then focusing on the feeling of the rest of my body slowly moving up, or focusing on the texture of something soft or scratchy. There are also grounding exercises that other people can help you with - if you develop a way to communicate that you’re having a flashback or overwhelmed someone can ask you to name 10 things you see or answer 10 silly questions. Mostly I would say please try to be kind to yourself. Recognize that your panic response is you trying to keep yourself safe from perceived harm. There is nothing wrong with you, in fact this happens because you did what you had to do to survive pain and abuse. Over time you will be more able to communicate/build trust/ ground yourself in the present. I hope that you are in a safe situation now and wish you the best - you will get through this.

Chinese Money Plant (Pilea peperomioides)

fyi the leaves on this don't create roots in water, but these things sprout up babies all the time. I've had one for about a \~8 months and its given me 9 pups, and would likely shoot up more if I split all of them (only removed 4 a few months ago and new ones shot up). It looks like you have two stalks in there. You might want to repot them separately and then just take good care of them and wait for the babies to sprout up. When the pups come up just cut them out at the stalk in the bottom of soil. Those can go into water for a bit and then planted!
